subject: Novacorp: Request to modify liability cap and warranty language
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@novacorps.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed contract adjustments and redlines

Jonas / Irene,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Attaching our latest redlines (Novacorp_Redlines_v3.docx). Two core asks from Legal/Procurement to get the internal sponsor comfortable: 

1) Liability cap: increase from standard $1M to $2M and carve out breaches of confidentiality/data incidents so we can pursue full direct damages in those circumstances.
2) Warranty: replace the standard "as-is" operational warranty with a 24-month limited performance warranty tied to uptime SLAs and a remedy ladder (service credits then termination).

We recognize these are non-standard. Novacorp is prepared to commit to a 24-month commercial term and a minimum committed spend of $450k upfront if we can get these concessions. The procurement team also asked whether Redwood would consider a 20% one-time onboarding credit to offset transition costs — not a recurring discount.

Can your team confirm whether these changes are acceptable, and if they require executive sign-off? We're hopeful to close by the end of May.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Novacorp
Attachments: Novacorp_Redlines_v3.docx

Subject: RE: Proposed contract adjustments and redlines

Looping you in — Novacorp has sent redlines that request two principal deviations from our standard form: raise the liability cap to $2M with a data-breach carveout, and a 24-month limited performance warranty. They pair this with a firm 24-month term and $450k upfront; they've also asked for a one-time 20% onboarding credit (pricing_summary.xlsx shows the math).

Quick context: Novacorp is a mid-enterprise in healthcare analytics (large potential ARR expansion once integrated). Deal desk has okayed the commercial terms if legal confirms risk. Irene, can you summarize risk tolerance and whether this meets our escalation threshold? Aditya, if legal needs an executive exception for liability/warranty, what information do you need to sign off?

I pasted Sarah's note below for reference. Attaching their redlines.

Thanks,
– Jonas

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed contract adjustments and redlines

Jonas — reviewed the redlines. Summary of legal stance and recommended escalation: 

- Liability cap: they're asking to double the cap and to carve out confidentiality/data incidents. We do not accept carveouts that remove cap for data incidents because that effectively leaves us unlimited exposure for security failures. If the customer insists on a carveout for data breaches, we need exec approval AND a plan: higher cap (>$2M), cyber insurance confirmation from Novacorp, and a reciprocal indemnity for claims caused by Novacorp's misuse of data.

- Warranty: the proposed 24-month performance warranty with SLA-linked credits and step-remedies is heavily operational and overlaps with our product guarantees. We can offer a limited 12-month warranty tied to documented SLAs and an engineering remediation commitment, but 24 months is a long tail. Offering 24 months increases exposure; requires exec approval and a detailed outage credit cap.

- Commercial tradeoff: $450k upfront is material. If we take the increased liability/warranty exposure, we should negotiate either a higher cap (pro-rated by term), a structured pricing uplift (to cover risk), or limit the credit request. A 20% one-time credit on onboarding for $450k is $90k — acceptable if paired with tightened indemnity language and an insurance certificate.

Recommendation: escalate to Aditya (CFO) / CEO for authorization to: (1) approve a $2M cap only if Novacorp provides proof of cyber insurance (min $5M) and (2) approve a 24-month warranty only if we cap aggregate credits at 10% of annual spend and include a termination right after two SLA misses in 12 months. Both require executive authority per our deal desk policy.

I can draft the conditional language for Risk to sign off if we get approval on the parameters above.

– Irene
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed contract adjustments and redlines

Thanks for the concise summary. A few financial points before I can authorize any exception: 

1) Margin impact: what is the expected ACV beyond the $450k upfront? Show 3-year ARR projection and incremental gross margin impact of granting the liability/warranty changes.
2) Risk mitigation: if we require Novacorp to present a $5M cyber insurance certificate and increase price by 7% for the added exposure, does that keep sales economics attractive?
3) Precedent: will approving a 24-month warranty open the door for similar requests from other healthcare customers? If so, we need a templated addendum.

Jonas — please send numbers and the final proposed language you want me to sign off on. If legal's conditions are codified (insurance + cap on credits + termination triggers), I'm willing to greenlight a $2M cap and the 24-month warranty, provided we have a 7% price uplift (or an equivalent non-recurring onboarding offset) and proof of insurance.

Aditya
CFO, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@novacorps.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@novacorps.com>
Date: 2026-04-23T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Novacorp proposal — consolidated ask and exec approval request

Aditya / Irene / Marissa — consolidating for exec review and approval. Below are the proposed, conditioned concessions Redwood would make, and the asks from Novacorp: 

Redwood conditional concessions (if Novacorp agrees):
- Liability cap: increase to $2M total liability, but NO unlimited carveout for data breaches. Condition: Novacorp provides cyber insurance certificate (min $5M) and we include reciprocal limitations for claims caused by Novacorp.
- Warranty: offer a 24-month limited performance warranty tied to documented SLAs. Cap aggregate service credits at 10% of annual contract value and include measurable termination triggers (two SLA misses in a 12-month rolling period).
- Pricing: apply a 7% one-time price uplift to offset risk OR allow the 20% onboarding credit but only if Novacorp accepts the price uplift on renewal and provides insurance.

Novacorp asks:
- Acceptance of the 24-month warranty and $2M cap with the data-breach carveout intact; and a 20% onboarding credit.

Net commercial: $450k upfront commitment + potential upsell corridor. Pricing_summary.xlsx attached shows revenue and margin with both uplift options. If approved, I will: (1) share the conditional redline language Irene drafts, (2) ask Novacorp to sign a DocuSign addendum (link), and (3) request their insurance certificate before countersignature.

Decision request to Aditya (exec): Please confirm whether you approve the conditional concessions (increase cap + 24-month warranty) under the terms above and whether you prefer the 7% uplift or allowing the 20% onboarding credit as the tradeoff. If approved, I'll instruct Legal to prepare the addendum and proceed to DocuSign.

Thanks — target close: end of May.

Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192
